outcomes: A repository that keeps its own CI describes one change, what it touches, its tests, its coverage and its dependency changes, in one versioned document that any reader interprets the same way.
A producer and every reader share one schema, one strict parser and one fixture corpus, so a document either validates everywhere or is refused with the same codes.
A document is internally consistent and bounded: every reference resolves, every count adds up, and no member grows without limit.
nonGoals: Collecting the reports, detecting components or computing the analyses, which the observe extension owns.
Uploading the document or deciding how much a reader trusts it: the document carries no verdict and no trust claim, and a reader treats it as self-reported.
Spec, architecture or task evidence, which later protocol versions or other protocols carry.

requirements.text: Documents are protocol version 1. The code host is github, gitlab or generic; the CI system is github-actions, gitlab-ci or generic; a component source is orchestrator, workspace, manifest, fallback or declared; a component impact is changed, dependent or unaffected; a file status is added, modified, deleted or renamed; a dependency change is added, removed, upgraded, downgraded or changed. Ecosystems are open lowercase slugs. Every validation code starts with evidence.
For every object, schemas/evidence.json declares exactly the members of the Go type, and so does the strict decoder's case-sensitive member walk. The schema's enums are the Go vocabularies.

fixtures/expectations.json lists exactly the fixtures on disk. The reader validates each valid fixture without an error and gives each invalid fixture exactly its listed distinct codes, all in the closed validation set.

The reader refuses with evidence.parse_error bytes that are not JSON, a second document after the first, a document that is not an object, or a member of the wrong type. A member the schema does not declare, at any depth and compared case-sensitively, is evidence.unknown_field at its dotted path.

The subject names its code host, its repository and a commit sha of 40 or 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters; a base sha, when present, has the same form. A github or gitlab subject also names its host and its numeric project id, the stable key that survives a rename. A change request number is positive. A CI run URL is https and carries no credentials. Any other subject or CI defect is evidence.invalid_subject or evidence.invalid_ci.

Every path is relative to the repository root, slash-separated, non-empty, with no leading slash, no backslash and no dot-dot segment; a component id is such a path or the root, written as a single dot. A renamed file names its previous path and no other status does. Any defect is evidence.invalid_path.

Component ids, changed file paths, and the components of tests and coverage entries are unique, else evidence.duplicate. Every component a changed file, a dependency edge, a tests or coverage entry or a dependency change names exists, else evidence.unknown_component.

A component is changed exactly when a changed file belongs to it; it is dependent exactly when it is not changed and reaches a changed component through its dependency edges; every other component is unaffected. Any other impact is evidence.invalid_impact.

Counts and durations are non-negative; covered lines never exceed total lines; a tests entry lists no more failing cases than it counts failures; the changed-line coverage totals are the sums of its files; uncovered line numbers are positive, strictly increasing, and no more than the file's uncovered lines. Any defect is evidence.invalid_count.

A dependency change names its ecosystem, its lockfile and its package. An added package has a to version and no from version, a removed one a from version and no to version, and every other change both versions, which differ. Any defect is evidence.invalid_dependency_change.

A document holds at most 20000 changed files, 5000 components, 10000 dependency changes, 20000 changed-line coverage files and 500 diagnostics; a tests entry at most 50 failing cases and a file at most 200 uncovered line numbers. A larger member is evidence.too_large. generatedAt is an RFC 3339 timestamp with a zone, else evidence.invalid_timestamp; a reader diagnostic has a known severity and a dotted code, else evidence.invalid_diagnostic.
